comments.text:
Hola.
Матушка Россия 😘🇷🇺
Madre Rusia sin principio ni fin.
Me enamoré en el '70 con ocho años por las carreras de moto sobre hielo, la escogí en el '71 por el libro "Mijail Stragiff de Jules Verne" y me crié con slavos; sobretodo polacos; supervivientes de los campos de exterminio "boches"; Austria-Alemania; y aquí sigo, del lado de Rusia y los Slavos.
Gracias por tan hermoso reportaje 12/10.
Sólo decirte que la mitad de las "O" que has pronunciado son "A", porque en ruso, toda "O" no acentuada, le pronuncia "A".
Vladivostok = Vladivastok. Moskva = Maskva. Volokolamsk = Valakalamsk. Moloko = Malako.
Y no hay excepciones.
¿Y por qué pronuncias los nombres rusos con acento estadounidense?. Es ruso, no inglés. 
Yo no digo Guasintong, ni güiski, ni Iogua.
Tal vez por eso a pesar de ser español, mi idioma materno es el francés, los franceses creen que soy francés y los españoles no se creen que me crié en francés.
Por lo demás СПАСИБО = СПАСИБА.
ПОЖАЛУЙСТА.

How Orthodoxy preserved Rus' (Russia)

Orthodoxy played a huge role in preserving Rus', especially during difficult periods in history. Here are the main ways it helped people maintain their culture, identity, and faith:

How Orthodoxy preserved Rus' (Russia)
Spiritual connection and culture: Orthodoxy became the foundation of Russian spiritual life, literature, iconography, architecture, and rituals. This strengthened a sense of unity and national identity.
Protection from invaders: During invasions and enemies, faith gave people hope and resilience.
Education and monastic heritage: Monasteries like Kyiv-Pechersk, Spaso-Preobrazhensky, established schools, libraries, and manuscripts, helping preserve knowledge and culture.
Confession and spiritual resistance: In the darkest times, faith gave strength and hope, inspiring heroism and resistance.
Examples of feats of faith (Christian heroic deeds)
The uprising in the Kremlin in 1612: The people organized a militia led by Minin and Pozharsky, which freed Moscow from Polish invaders. This act strengthened faith in the victory of the Russian nation and Orthodoxy.

Heroic deed of Alexander Svirsky: A monk and miracle worker who served for many years in difficult conditions, helping people, maintaining faith, and demonstrating spiritual resilience.

Easter 1240 — the seizure of Kyiv: During this difficult time, many Christians continued to hold their faith and pray despite the city's destruction.

Martyrdom of saints and martyrs: Many saints and martyrs, such as Princess Catherine or Saint Sergius of Radonezh, accepted death or suffering for their faith, remaining examples of spiritual steadfastness.
